name: Primo G. Garcia
half:
Primo G. Garcia has advised 8 theses in this repository between 2021 and 2026. Their research supervision covers a broad range of topics, with the most frequent areas of focus being governance and public policy, gender and inclusion, business and entrepreneurship, and management and leadership. Other supervised topics include agriculture and food, community development, public health and COVID-19, climate and disaster, communication studies, and science education.

The adviser's supervision patterns show a recent concentration of work in 2026, including studies on rice farming technology adoption, customer experience in utility business centers, and digital R&D procedures in manufacturing. Earlier supervision includes work on organizational structures for tobacco research, discourse analysis of ASEAN disaster management speeches, and the economic impacts of foreign direct investment in ASEAN member states. They have also supervised research regarding fiscal policy impacts on inclusive growth and the persistence of Filipino-American students in biology majors. Additionally, Garcia has authored one article in this repository from 2018 concerning student attrition in distance education. Based on the available items, their strengths as an adviser appear to lie in multidisciplinary studies involving ASEAN regional policy, organizational management, and social inclusion issues. Evidence regarding their specific academic degrees or formal institutional affiliations is not provided in the fact sheet.

Their research supervision covers a wide range of sub-topics, with the most frequent areas of focus being governance and public policy (3), gender and inclusion (3), business and entrepreneurship (2), and management and leadership (2). Other supervised topics include agriculture and food (1), community development (1), public health and COVID-19 (1), climate and disaster (1), communication studies (1), and science education (1). Garcia has an advisee in the latest year recorded in the repository, 2026.

In the 2026 academic year, Garcia supervised three theses. These works addressed diverse areas including agriculture and food through a study on the Riceboost Initiative Package of Technology's impact on rice farmers, business and entrepreneurship via research into customer experience and digital adoption at an electric company, and management and leadership through an investigation into stage-gate standard operating procedures for digital R&D in a manufacturing firm. In 2025, Garcia advised a thesis regarding stakeholder perceptions of organizational structures for a proposed tobacco research and grading institute in the Philippines, which touched upon management and leadership and public health and COVID-19.

Earlier supervision in 2022 included three theses. These covered governance and public policy and communication studies through a discourse analysis of ASEAN member states' speeches on natural disasters, business and entrepreneurship and governance and public policy through a study on the effects of foreign direct investment on ASEAN economic growth, and governance and public policy and gender and inclusion through an assessment of fiscal policy's impacts on inclusive growth and income redistribution in ASEAN member states. In 2021, Garcia supervised a phenomenological study on the persistence of Filipino-American students in undergraduate biology majors, which falls under science education and gender and inclusion.

In addition to thesis supervision, Garcia has one article in this repository from 2018, which analyzed the reasons for students filing for leave of absence or dropping courses within the Faculty of Management and Development Studies, specifically focusing on gender and inclusion and online and distance learning. Based on the available data, Garcia's supervision pattern shows a strong interest in regional ASEAN issues, governance, and social inclusion, with a recent expansion into specific organizational management and agricultural technology topics. The breadth of topics suggests experience in guiding qualitative exploratory studies, discourse analysis, and quantitative investigations such as multiple regression analysis.
